attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his newsletter, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: The wording is accurate. But 'basically' and 'obvious' make this an evaluative, hyperbolic judgment rather than a measurable observation. 'Basically' openly allows exceptions without saying how many or how large.

contract.note: The contract treats any single substantial non-coding application as a contradiction. That turns 'basically the only obvious' into 'no other established use', which is stretched against the speaker. The speaker gave no measure for 'obvious' or for how many exceptions 'basically' allows.

evidence.note: Duolingo's own disclosure that the Video Call feature was available in September 2025. It shows a deployment, not independently verified usefulness, and one feature cannot settle an evaluative 'basically'.
Company blog post from April 2025 showing the feature runs on an LLM. It is background only.
Duolingo's own summary of its efficacy study. It is a company disclosure, not an independent finding, and does not cover the target period.
Reuters reports Klarna scaling back its AI emphasis. This is a caution about non-coding deployments, not a test of the claim.

reviews.rationale: The statement is an evaluative, hyperbolic judgment. 'Obvious' has no measure, and 'basically' allows unspecified exceptions. The contract reads a single non-coding deployment as a contradiction, which is not a fair ordinary reading. The only counterexample offered is a single company-disclosed feature with company-reported efficacy. It cannot fairly decide whether coding is 'basically the only obvious' use case.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence, introduced with 'I need to be blunter'.

semantics.note: This is a compound of present-tense assessments and a 'will burn' forecast. The summary omits that the deals exceed the venture capital and private credit available, but the core commitments are kept. No deadline is given.

contract.note: The contract treats the claim as compound, requires every component for support, and reports partial findings separately. Its readings of 'burn' and 'profitability' are fair and ordinary.

evidence.note: SoftBank's own disclosure that it completed a $30B investment in OpenAI. It shows some capital was raised, but not that all the identified commitments are funded or paid.
Secondary report of OpenAI's own projection of $278B negative free cash flow for 2026–2030. A projection is not realized burn and covers a different basis.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and no conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule. There is no completed funding and payment of the commitments, no sustained profitability, no realized burn near $300B, and no liquidation. The SoftBank financing and the FT-reported projection are context only.

semantics.note: The survival antecedent and the 'by 2029' horizon are kept. 'From what I can tell' states the basis for his view, not graded probability, so the firm 'will have burned' is scorable.

contract.note: Measuring cumulative negative free cash flow over 2025–2029 matches the surrounding projection table. Taking the latest reasonable deadline is fair to the speaker.

evidence.note: A 2026–2030 projection, not realized cash flow, and for a different period than the claim. It can neither support nor contradict.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2029) is after the evaluation date. Whether the antecedent (OpenAI surviving) holds is unknown, and no realized cash-flow record covers the period. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words: 'which I do not believe it will'.

semantics.note: 'I do not believe it will' is an unqualified belief, not graded low or medium confidence, so it is scored as a forecast. The horizon is 2029.

contract.note: Survival means continued business operation, and restructuring alone does not count as failure. Taking the latest deadline and allowing early support only on a documented shutdown are fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own October 2026 announcement shows ongoing commercial activity. That does not establish survival through 2029.

reviews.rationale: The deadline (end of 2029) has not arrived, and the evidence records no permanent cessation or liquidation that would meet the early-resolution rule. Continued operation before the deadline cannot contradict the forecast early, so it is not yet scorable.
